analyst_view.overall: Club Brugge and Liverpool are level on 9 points (9th and 8th), so a win puts either close to the top eight. Brugge, under Ivan Leko, have won their last three in Europe and scored freely; striker Nicolo Tresoldi is over his concussion and Freddie Potts is back from a domestic ban. Liverpool, now coached by Andoni Iraola, have been patchy but get Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong back, with Dominik Szoboszlai fit; Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni look too early and Hugo Ekitike is still out with his long-term Achilles injury. The numbers list nobody missing and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting, and no referee is named yet. Liverpool host Manchester United on Sunday, so some rotation is possible but nothing has been said.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already add a little for Brugge's 17 goals in their last 6. Liverpool are close to full strength apart from Ekitike, who has been out since April and so is already reflected in their recent games, and Brugge have Tresoldi back. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.2 corners, 6 of them Liverpool's, and already add about 3% for Liverpool's high corner count lately. With Frimpong back on the right, Liverpool's wide play should look like it has in their recent games, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.1 cards and already add about 6% for Brugge's recent cards and take a little off Liverpool's. The referee is not named yet and there is no rivalry between the clubs. I stay at about 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.4 shots and have already pushed both sides up by 15-17% for their recent shooting. Gravenberch and Szoboszlai back in midfield fit that picture rather than add to it, so I see no reason to go further and stay at 34.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target, already up for Brugge's sharp finishing (+8%) and Liverpool's volume. Both attacks are near full strength, with Tresoldi back for Brugge and Ekitike's long absence already in Liverpool's form, so I stay at 11.5.
